prompt: Stage 4-5, level 7 with 62 gold and 55 HP on a 2-loss streak, losing about 12 HP a round. Your 4-cost carry and 4-cost tank are 1-star with items; your 3-cost caster is one copy from 2-star. Level 8 costs 20 XP. Do you level to 8 and roll, roll at 7, or hold for 5-1?

options.label: Level to 8 (20 gold) and roll the remaining 42 for the two 4-costs; 62 is enough to do both
Roll at 7: 3-costs are 43% here against 32% at 8, and the caster 2-star is the closest upgrade
Hold 62, level 8 at 5-1 with 80 and roll then

explanation:
Roll where the units that change your fights live: the 1-star 4-costs. At level 7 a 4-cost is 10% of a slot; at 8 it is 30%. Sixty-two gold at 7 is thirty-one shops, 155 slots, about 15 four-cost slots. Twenty for the level and 42 rolled at 8 is twenty-one shops, 105 slots, about 32 four-cost slots: two thirds of the gold, twice the 4-costs, and an eighth unit on the board. The caster upgrade is not lost; 3-costs are still 32% at 8 and you need one copy.

This is the case where levelling and rolling in the same round is right: 62 leaves more than 40 to roll after the level, still a real rolldown.

Holding to 5-1 is the tempting greed at 55 HP. Two more losses at 12 to 13 put you near 30 entering stage 5, where a loss costs 20: two losses from elimination with the same board. The extra 18 gold at 5-1 is not worth 25 HP.
principle: Roll where the units that change your fights live: for 4-costs that is level 8, and at 60 gold you can afford to get there and roll.
commonMistake: Rolling at 7 because the 3-cost odds look better, and finding 3-costs on a board that loses because its 4-costs are 1-star.
hint: Count the 4-cost slots your gold shows at 7 versus at 8 after paying for the level.
